top_story: Israeli policy debate has shifted from coercive pressure to openly articulated mass expulsion, with Defence Minister Israel Katz seeking Donald Trump’s backing on 2 September and Itamar Ben-Gvir formalizing the next day a $20 billion, seven-year plan to remove all Palestinians from Gaza as a coalition condition. That escalation matters beyond rhetoric because it aligns cabinet politics with a program of demographic engineering that would harden displacement as a governing objective rather than a wartime byproduct. In the West Bank, this political trajectory is mirrored on the ground by armed settler incursions into villages such as Qira and by a sharp rise in settler and soldier violence that has killed at least 76 Palestinians in 2026, the deadliest year yet recorded. Together, these developments point to a widening Israeli effort to reorder Palestinian presence across Gaza and the West Bank through both formal planning and cumulative coercion, with severe implications for civilian survival and any remaining political horizon.
